title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Internal Tools
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Overview

This page is the canonical company handbook section for new and existing employees about: what it means to work at Redwood, our role and level framework, career ladder expectations, key benefits and perks, hiring and onboarding overview, and an at-a-glance guide to internal tools. It is maintained by People Ops and is intended for all Redwood employees. For team-specific variations (e.g., individual compensation bands, team level calibrations), consult your manager or the People Ops team.

1) Working at Redwood - culture and expectations

Summary:
- Mission-first, product-minded engineering culture: we prioritize predictable, production-grade inference and developer-first tooling.
- Respectful, inclusive collaboration: psychological safety, feedback loops, and asynchronous-first communication.
- Outcome-oriented, data-informed decision making: owners are expected to measure impact and iterate.

Key principles:
- Ship with care: prioritize reliability and observability in every change.
- Communicate clearly: use Confluence and RFCs for design decisions; keep teammates informed via Slack and PR descriptions.
- Growth mindset: expect continuous improvement in craft and cross-functional skills.

Day-to-day expectations:
- Regular 1:1s with managers (recommended cadence 1:1 weekly or biweekly).
- Quarterly goals (OKRs or equivalent) aligned to product and company-level themes.
- Participation in peer reviews, design reviews, and cross-team syncs as relevant.

2) Roles & Career Ladders

Purpose:
- Provide transparent expectations for levels, promotion criteria, and typical responsibilities. Teams may add role-specific supplements (e.g., infra, product, research).

Core levels (company-wide standard):
| Level | Common title examples | Summary responsibilities | Typical impact scope |
|-------|-----------------------|--------------------------|----------------------|
| IC1   | Jr Software Engineer, Associate | Contributes to tasks with mentorship, learns codebase and practices | Component-level |
| IC2   | Software Engineer | Owns features, participates in design, reliable delivery | Multi-component / single service |
| IC3   | Senior Software Engineer | Leads feature design, mentors others, drives technical decisions | Service-level / cross-service |
| IC4   | Staff Software Engineer | Shapes architecture, leads cross-team initiatives, sets technical direction | Multi-team / product area |
| IC5+  | Principal / Distinguished | Company-level technical leadership, long-term platform strategy | Company-wide or industry influence |

Engineering manager ladder:
- EM1 (Manager): people manager for small teams, responsible for delivery and growth of direct reports.
- EM2 (Senior Manager): manages managers or larger teams, cross-team delivery and career development.
- EM3+ (Director / VP): broader organizational leadership and strategy.

Promotion rubric (summary):
- Evidence of consistent impact over 3-6 months (IC promotions often require sustained outcomes over multiple quarters).
- Demonstrated ownership and independent judgement at the next level.
- Positive peer feedback and measurable product or reliability improvements.
- Manager & calibration committee approval.

Career development resources:
- Quarterly calibration & promotion cycles; speak with manager by mid-quarter about promotion readiness.
- Learning stipend: see Benefits section for learning & conference allowances.
- Mentorship program and internal tech talks.

3) Benefits & Perks (summary)

Health and wellbeing:
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with company-subsidized premiums (US, EMEA-appropriate variants available).
- Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and mental health counseling benefits.
- Wellness stipend (annual).

Time off and leave:
- Paid Time Off (PTO): flexible vacation policy with manager-aligned coverage (recommended minimum use: 15 business days/year).
- Company holidays: 10-12 days depending on region.
- Parental leave: primary caregiver 18 weeks, secondary caregiver 8 weeks (regional variations & legal requirements apply).
- Domestic and international sick leave per local laws.

Financial & retirement:
- Competitive base salary and equity grants at hire; annual refreshes for eligible roles.
- 401(k) matching for US employees (plan details in Benefits portal).

Learning & growth:
- Learning stipend: up to $2,000/year for courses, conferences, books, certifications.
- Paid time for internal training and brown-bag tech talks.

Remote & office work:
- Hybrid-friendly with core collaboration expectations; teams define in-person meeting cadence.
- Home office stipend for remote equipment and ergonomic needs.

Other perks:
- Commuter benefits (where applicable), monthly wellness credits, and regular company socials and hackweeks.

How to file benefits requests or questions:
1. Visit the Benefits portal (link on the People Ops Confluence home).
2. For ambiguous cases (regional variations, special accommodations), contact benefits@redwood.com and People Ops.

4) Hiring & Onboarding overview

Hiring process (high level):
1. Requisition and approval: hiring manager opens req with Business Case and Headcount approval.
2. Sourcing & screening: Talent partners prioritize diversity and role-fit; initial phone screen by recruiter.
3. Hiring loop: a structured onsite/virtual loop composed of technical assessment, system design or role-specific exercise, collaboration/culture interview, and manager interview.
4. Offer & negotiation: compensation is set by People Ops with manager input; offers include base salary, equity, and benefits summary.
5. Background checks & onboarding paperwork: initiated after candidate accepts.

Interview guidelines (for interviewers):
- Use the standard interview template (job-specific rubric + behavioral questions).
- Provide written feedback within 48 hours; score consistently against rubric.
- Avoid asking for irrelevant personal information; follow security & compliance guidance for acceptable interview questions.

Onboarding (first 90 days):
Week 0 (pre-start):
- New hire receives welcome packet, equipment checklist, and first-week schedule.
Day 1-7:
- Orientation: HR intro, benefits enrollment, security training, and account setup (Okta, Slack, VPN).
- Team onboarding: meet manager, set 30/60/90 goals, pair with an onboarding buddy.
Month 1:
- Deliver a small onboarding project or documentation task.
- Check-ins: weekly 1:1s and team sync.
Month 2-3:
- Increased ownership of tasks; participate in prioritization and planning.
- 90-day review with manager to capture progress and goals.

Hiring & offer contacts:
- Primary recruiter: see People Ops directory.
- Compensation and equity questions: comp@redwood.com.

5) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

Purpose: provides the essential tools and first-step instructions for daily work. For detailed, tool-specific runbooks, see eng-developer-experience and eng-infra spaces.

Access and identity:
- Okta (SSO): primary identity provider for all apps. Request app access via Okta request flow; manager approval required for sensitive apps.
- IAM & cloud accounts: cloud access requires manager approval and security training. See eng-infra/courtship checklist.

Communication & collaboration:
- Slack: primary async communication; channels organized by team and product area. Use channel naming conventions: #<team>-<topic> or #product-<area>.
- Confluence: canonical documentation store. This handbook lives under /company-handbook.
- Google Workspace: docs, sheets, slides for collaborative drafts; finalize important specs to Confluence.

Engineering tools:
- GitHub: main repo hosting and PR workflows. Branch naming: team/feature-<short-desc>. All changes require at least one approving review and CI green.
- CI/CD: primary pipeline is in the eng-infra CI project; follow the CI runbook for flake troubleshooting and secrets handling.
- Internal CLI: redwoodctl (developer bootstrap, deploy, logs) - see quickstart in eng-developer-experience.

Observability & incidents:
- Dashboards: Grafana links in eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts.
- Error tracking: Sentry for application errors; populate issues and tag oncall.
- PagerDuty: primary alerting for oncall rotation; ensure the responder schedule is kept current.

HR & finance systems:
- Payroll & expenses: use Expensify (or local equivalent) for reimbursement and travel.
- Time off: submit PTO via the People Ops portal; manager approval required for extended leaves.

Getting help & escalation:
- For access issues: submit request through the IT Helpdesk (link in Confluence) or ping #it-support.
- For payroll or benefits escalations: benefits@redwood.com and people-ops@redwood.com.
- For security incidents: follow the incident process in security-and-compliance/incident-response-security and alert security@redwood.com immediately.

6) Governance, ownership and revision history

Document ownership:
- Maintained by People Ops (owner: People Ops Handbook team). For technical accuracy in tooling sections, eng-developer-experience and eng-infra are co-reviewers.

Review cadence:
- Annual review by People Ops with quarterly quick checks for tooling or policy changes. Major updates coordinated with Legal, Security, and Finance as required.

Change log (recent):
- 2026-04-01: Initial published handbook consolidated onboarding, roles, and benefits (Ava Thompson).
- 2027-02-15: Updated parental leave policy, learning stipend amounts, and added new redwoodctl quickstart link (Ava Thompson).

How to request changes:
1. Open a Confluence edit request on this page and tag @people-ops.
2. For policy-level changes (comp/leave/benefits), include a business rationale and identify stakeholders.
